correctness.rationale: For n>=9 the Parseval vectors v_{ij}=(e_i+e_j-2/n 1)/sqrt(n-2) form the stated edge-indexed frame; their full Gram is (|e∩f|-4/n)/(n-2). A matching M of t erased edges has H=2/(n-2)I-4/[n(n-2)]J. The Woodbury identity yields Q=P_EE+P_EM(I-H)^(-1)P_ME and the explicit entry formula in RESULT.md. Its sign is determined by whether retained edges intersect; orbit-wise row sums depend on erased-incidence s_e=0,1,2. The maximal incidence row gives the three rational branches of Lambda_{n,t}. Exact differences have the common n²-12n+24 factor, negative at n=9 and positive at all integer n>=10, and derivative in t is strictly negative after t=2. I built and inverted exact rational deletion Grams independently for every matching size at n=9,10,11,12; resulting max-row norms agree. This concerns canonical Parseval renormalization only, not the best possible complement projection.
residual_risks: All-erased configurations are required to be matchings. At n=9 the optimal matching size is zero; positive t reduces norm. No claims below n=9 or for arbitrary deletion graphs.
